questions.question_text: A student attempts to solve the equation \(\cos x + \sin x \tan x = 2 \sin x - 1\) in the range \(0 \leq x \leq 2\pi\). The student’s attempt is as follows: \(\cos x + \sin x \tan x = 2 \sin x - 1\) So \(\cos x - \sin x + \sin x \tan x - \sin x = -1\) (I) So \((\sin x - \cos x)(\tan x - 1) = -1\) (II) So \(\sin x - \cos x = -1\) or \(\tan x - 1 = -1\) (III) So \((\sin x - \cos x)^{2} = 1\) or \(\tan x = 0\) (IV) So \(2 \sin x \cos x = 0\) or \(\tan x = 0\) (V) So \(x = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\) (VI) Which of the following best describes this attempt?

options.B: It is incorrect, and the first error occurs on line (I)
options.C: It is incorrect, and the first error occurs on line (II)
options.D: It is incorrect, and the first error occurs on line (III)
options.E: It is incorrect, and the first error is that extra solutions were introduced on line (IV)
options.F: It is incorrect, and the first error is that extra solutions were introduced on line (V)
options.G: It is incorrect, and the first error is not eliminating the values where \(\tan x\) is undefined on line (VI)

        So   sin x − cos x = −1 or tan x − 1 = −1                             (III)
        So   (sin x − cos x)2 = 1 or tan x = 0                                (IV)
        So   2 sin x cos x = 0 or tan x = 0                                   (V)
